patches.old: it has two lone pairs (one in an sp² orbital, one in the unhybridized p orbital participating in the pi bond)
patches.new: it has two lone pairs, and both of them occupy sp² orbitals in the molecular plane (the unhybridized p orbital is already committed to the pi bond, so it cannot also hold a lone pair)
patches.reason: Orbital-counting error. In an sp² oxygen the unhybridized p orbital contributes its single electron to the pi bond; both non-bonding pairs sit in sp² hybrid orbitals. Chemguide/LibreTexts: two of the sp² hybrid orbitals contain the lone pairs. Lone-pair location on carbonyl oxygen is directly testable (nucleophilicity, protonation site, n to pi* transitions).

patches.old: Carbonyl oxygen: **sp²** (one lone pair in sp² orbital, one in p orbital)
patches.new: Carbonyl oxygen: **sp²** (both lone pairs in sp² orbitals; the p orbital is used for the pi bond)
patches.reason: Same error repeated in the functional-group quick reference; corrected to match the body text.

patches.old: (sp character pulls electrons toward carbon, partially shielding the proton)
patches.new: (the electronegative sp carbon deshields, but the cylindrical pi electron cloud of the triple bond shields the proton more strongly, so the net shift is upfield of vinyl protons)
patches.reason: The stated mechanism is backwards: pulling electron density toward carbon deshields the proton and would predict a downfield shift. The observed upfield position comes from diamagnetic anisotropy, the induced field of the cylindrical pi cloud opposing the applied field along the triple-bond axis, which outweighs the sp-carbon deshielding (JoVE Core Analytical Chemistry 8.5).

A lower panel works through a carbonyl oxygen, where one sigma bond plus two lone pairs gives sp2 and both lone pairs occupy sp2 orbitals because the unhybridized p orbital is already used by the pi bond.
